title: Distributed Replicated Key-Value Store from Scratch in Go with Raft Consensus, LevelDB WAL & gRPC Cluster Transport
problem: Single-point-of-failure database architectures suffer from catastrophic outages, data corruption, and prolonged downtime when server hardware fails or network partitions isolate data centers. Off-the-shelf distributed stores obscure consensus mechanics, leaving software engineers unprepared to diagnose split-brain anomalies, phantom reads, and cascading leader failover storms. This project builds a production-grade distributed replicated key-value storage engine from scratch in Go implementing the Raft consensus algorithm. The engine implements randomized election timers, leader heartbeats, persistent write-ahead logging (WAL) using LevelDB, gRPC peer-to-peer RPC transport, cluster membership changes, log compaction via snapshotting, and linearizable read/write request semantics.

use_cases.title: Mission-Critical Distributed Configuration Management
use_cases.first_sentence: Cloud infrastructure control planes require a distributed configuration registry to coordinate microservice routing tables and database connection strings.
use_cases.second_sentence: The Raft cluster replicates configuration key-value pairs across 5 server nodes, guaranteeing linearizable reads and continuous availability even if 2 nodes fail.

use_cases.title: Distributed Lock Manager & Leader Election Coordinator
use_cases.first_sentence: High-throughput message processing workers require mutual exclusion distributed locks to prevent multiple worker nodes from processing the same queue partition.
use_cases.second_sentence: The key-value engine manages atomic compare-and-swap lease keys with TTL expirations, electing single active partition masters with zero split-brain risk.

use_cases.title: Distributed Service Discovery Registry & Health Tracker
use_cases.first_sentence: Dynamic container platforms need a resilient service discovery catalog that updates service instance IP endpoints as pods spawn and terminate.
use_cases.second_sentence: Service agents register ephemeral keys via gRPC client sessions, automatically replicating instance state across the Raft consensus quorum with low commit latency.

hard_parts: Implementing the Raft state machine transitions (Follower, Candidate, Leader) with thread-safe goroutine channels and randomized election timeouts
Enforcing the Raft Log Matching and Leader Completeness safety invariants during out-of-order AppendEntries RPC retries
Implementing LevelDB write-ahead log persistence and state snapshotting to truncate committed logs and prevent disk saturation
Handling complex cluster network partitions (minority vs majority split-brain) while guaranteeing linearizability and client request redirection
screener_signals: Clean Go codebase cleanly separating the Raft consensus state machine, gRPC RPC transport, LevelDB storage engine, and client API handlers
Chaos network partition benchmark report demonstrating automatic leader re-election in < 350ms upon primary leader termination

Anti-fake verification script partitioning 2 nodes of a 5-node cluster, writing 20 key-value pairs to the majority partition, healing the partition, and asserting the minority catches up with identical log state

architecture.data_flow: A client sends a Put(key, value) request to node 1; if node 1 is a follower, it returns the current leader's gRPC address; client redirects request to leader node 2; leader appends the command to its local log and persists to LevelDB; leader sends AppendEntries RPCs containing the new entry to all followers over gRPC; once a majority (3 of 5 nodes) acknowledge replication, the leader advances its commitIndex, applies the entry to the state machine, and replies success to the client; during subsequent heartbeats, followers learn of the new commitIndex and apply the entry to their local state machines.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Raft Election Safety invariant ensuring at most one leader per term; strict quorum write replication (majority = N/2 + 1).

targets.method: Wall-clock timing from abrupt leader termination (SIGKILL) to successful election of new cluster leader across 5 nodes
targets.input: 10 repeated leader termination trials injected during active client traffic
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Go 1.21+ release binary, 5-node local cluster communicating over loopback ports
targets.minimum_pass: p95 leader election failover latency is < 450 milliseconds
targets.target: p95 leader election failover latency is < 220 milliseconds
targets.report: Leader election failover latency summary and cluster transition log

targets.method: Committed key-value write transactions per second replicated across majority quorum and persisted to LevelDB
targets.input: 10,000 sequential Put requests issued across 20 concurrent client worker goroutines
targets.environment: 5-node local Raft cluster with LevelDB synchronous write options enabled
targets.minimum_pass: Sustained write throughput is >= 1,500 operations per second
targets.target: Sustained write throughput is >= 4,200 operations per second
targets.report: Raft cluster write throughput benchmark report and latency distribution

targets.metric: Network Partition Recovery Log Consistency Rate
targets.method: Verification of identical log entry sequences and state machine key-value pairs across all nodes after partition healing
targets.input: Network partition isolating 2 nodes for 30 seconds while 100 writes are committed to the 3-node majority partition
targets.environment: Automated network chaos test runner injecting TCP connection drop filters between cluster nodes
targets.minimum_pass: 5 of 5 nodes achieve identical state machine hash and log parity after partition healing
targets.target: 5 of 5 nodes achieve identical state machine hash and log parity after partition healing
targets.report: Network partition chaos test log and state checksum verification report

prerequisites: Proficiency in Go systems programming, goroutines, mutex synchronization, and channel communication
Deep understanding of distributed consensus concepts, state machine replication, and gRPC/Protobuf protocols

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU, memory, and disk I/O bound systems software)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Go 1.21+ release compiler and LevelDB dependencies installed
environment.fallback_path: In-memory append-only slice persistence if LevelDB CGO bindings encounter compilation hurdles

riskiest_component.name: Deadlocks in Concurrent State Transitions and Split-Brain Split-Votes
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce strict lock acquisition hierarchies, randomized election timeouts (150-300ms), and buffered event channels.
riskiest_component.fallback: Watchdog supervisor goroutine detecting lock stalls exceeding 1 second and dumping goroutine stack traces.

deliverables: Git repository containing Go Raft implementation, gRPC cluster server, LevelDB storage driver, and CLI client
Automated unit test suite verifying election safety, log matching invariants, and commit progression
Cluster chaos test harness simulating network partitions and measuring failover latency percentiles
Screener verification script executing automated 5-node cluster election and partition healing in under 3 minutes
out_of_scope: Multi-Raft sharding or distributed range partition architectures (CockroachDB style)
Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) algorithms handling malicious adversarial nodes
resources: In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Ongaro and Ousterhout - Raft Paper)
Raft Protocol Interactive Visualization (The Secret Lives of Data)
Students' Guide to Raft (Jon Gjengset Architecture Reference)

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a distributed replicated key-value storage engine in Go implementing Raft consensus, LevelDB WAL, and gRPC transport.
worksheet.q2: Target users: distributed systems engineers, infrastructure software developers, and database architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: distributed configuration management, distributed lock manager/leader coordinator, and dynamic service discovery.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: thread-safe Raft state transitions, AppendEntries safety invariants, LevelDB log compaction/snapshots, and partition chaos.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: Raft interfaces, gRPC protobufs, LevelDB wrapper, and cluster chaos runner. Synthetic test data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU/disk bound, $0 cost, zero cloud keys. Fallback: in-memory slice store.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: state transition deadlocks and split-vote ties. Fallback: randomized 150-300ms timers and deadlock watchdog.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: single-node key-value store pretending to be Raft. Anti-fake check 5 partitions 2 nodes, commits 20 writes to majority, heals, and asserts identical state hash.
worksheet.q10: Safe; synthetic configuration keys and private loopback network ports only.
